job.title: Payroll Officer
job.description:
Part-Time | Fixed-Term Maternity Leave Cover | 3 Days per Week

Bring your payroll expertise to a role that makes a difference.
Are you an experienced Payroll Officer who loves getting the details right, takes pride in delivering an exceptional service, and wants your work to contribute to something meaningful?

Lifeline WA is seeking a capable, proactive and people-focused Payroll Officer to join our team on a fixed-term maternity leave contract. This is an opportunity to take ownership of end-to-end payroll in a purpose-driven organisation, supporting the people who help make a difference in the lives of others.

Working three full days per week, you'll play an important role in ensuring our people are paid accurately and on time, while maintaining strong payroll controls, compliance and records. You'll be part of a collaborative team that values trust, respect, connection and excellence.

The opportunity

  • Start date: Ideally 4 January 2027
  • Contract: Fixed-term maternity leave cover through to 30 June 2028
  • Working days: Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday — all three days are essential.

What you'll be doing You'll coordinate accurate, timely and compliant fortnightly payroll for approximately 170 employees, including around 70 full-time staff and 100 Crisis Supporters who are paid based on timesheets.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Managing the end-to-end fortnightly payroll cycle, ensuring employees are paid accurately and on time.
  • Maintaining employee payroll records, including new starters, contract changes, pay point progressions, allowances, deductions, leave and terminations.
  • Applying your knowledge of the SCHADS Award to support accurate pay calculations and compliant payroll outcomes.
  • Administering payroll systems, investigating discrepancies and resolving payroll exceptions.
  • Completing payroll journals, payments, statutory lodgements, reporting and reconciliations.
  • Managing month-end payroll processes and associated balance sheet reconciliations.
  • Maintaining complete payroll documentation, audit trails and strong internal controls.
  • Responding to employee and manager enquiries with professionalism, discretion and a service-focused approach.

Ideally, you'll bring:

  • At least three years' experience in end-to-end payroll processing.
  • Strong working knowledge of the SCHADS Award and relevant payroll compliance requirements will be highly regarded.
  • Experience managing fortnightly payroll for a diverse workforce, including timesheet-based employees.
  • Experience with ELMO and confidence navigating payroll and HR systems.
  • Practical experience with payroll reconciliations, journals, lodgements, reporting and month-end processes.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to investigate and resolve payroll discrepancies.
  • Excellent attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities within tight deadlines.
  • Above all, you'll bring a positive attitude, a proactive mindset and a genuine commitment to being part of a supportive, values-driven team.


Interviews are expected to commence in the next few weeks so please apply today!

If you’re interested in this opportunity, please get in touch with Karen McGlynn on 0406 833 625 or email karen.mcglynn@aandco.au with your updated resume.

job.title: Chief Operating Officer
job.description:
InCasa Aged Care & Community Services is seeking an experienced and commercially astute Chief Operating Officer to join their leadership team.

Reporting directly to the CEO, this newly created role will take ownership of the operational performance of the organisation and play a key role in driving growth, efficiency, service excellence, and financial sustainability.

This is an opportunity for a proven aged care leader to step into a broad role with accountability across service delivery, workforce performance, quality, client experience, and operational outcomes.

About the Role

As COO, you will lead the day to day operations of the business, ensuring services are delivered effectively, efficiently, and in line with the organisation's strategic objectives.

You will establish clear performance frameworks and KPIs across the organisation, drive operational excellence, and identify opportunities to improve service delivery, productivity, financial performance, and customer outcomes.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Providing leadership across all operational functions.
  • Driving business performance through the development and monitoring of key operational and financial KPIs.
  • Overseeing workforce planning, scheduling, rostering, intake, care planning, and service delivery.
  • Ensuring high standards of quality, compliance, governance, and risk management.
  • Leading operational readiness and continuous improvement initiatives as the aged care sector continues to evolve.
  • Partnering with the CEO on strategic planning, growth opportunities, and organisational performance.

About You

You are a senior leader who understands both operations and finance and knows how to turn strategy into results.

You have successfully led large operational teams within the aged care sector and possess strong commercial acumen, financial management capability, and a track record of improving business performance.

You will bring:

  • Senior leadership experience within aged care, home care, community services, or a related health sector.
  • Strong financial literacy with the ability to manage budgets, analyse performance, and drive profitability and sustainability.
  • Experience leading large multidisciplinary teams across complex service environments.
  • A deep understanding of aged care operations, quality standards, compliance, and customer service.
  • Demonstrated success implementing KPIs, performance frameworks, and operational improvement initiatives.
  • Exceptional stakeholder engagement and leadership capability.

Why Join InCasa?

This is a rare opportunity to join a growing organisation and play a pivotal role in shaping its future. You will work alongside an engaged CEO and leadership team while having genuine influence over strategy, operations, culture, and performance.

If you are an experienced aged care leader looking for an opportunity to drive meaningful impact and help guide an organisation through its next phase of growth, we would welcome your application.

job.title: HR Consultant
job.description:
We are partnering with a well-established and highly respected WA-based consulting business that has been supporting organisations across a diverse range of industries for more than 25 years.

Working directly with business owners, executives and operational leaders, you'll have the opportunity to deliver meaningful HR solutions that help businesses navigate complex people challenges and drive organisational success.

As an HR Consultant, you'll manage a portfolio of clients across a range of industries, providing strategic and operational HR support across the full employee lifecycle.

From employee relations matters and workplace investigations through to organisational change, leadership development, policy development and workforce planning, you'll play a key role in helping clients achieve their people and business objectives.

This is a genuine consulting role that offers exposure to diverse organisations, projects and challenges while building strong relationships with leaders and key stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

  • Provide strategic and operational HR consulting services across a diverse client portfolio
  • Identify, develop and deliver tailored HR solutions aligned with client objectives
  • Advise on employee relations matters, performance management, disciplinary processes and workplace investigations
  • Provide guidance on Industrial Relations matters, including Awards, enterprise agreements and employment legislation
  • Develop and implement HR policies, procedures and frameworks aligned with best practice
  • Support workforce planning, talent management and recruitment initiatives
  • Conduct HR audits, reviews and organisational assessments
  • Facilitate training, leadership development and capability-building initiatives
  • Analyse workforce data and HR metrics to provide meaningful business insights
  • Support organisational change, restructures and transformation projects
  • Design and implement employee engagement and retention initiatives
  • Manage client relationships, project deliverables and consulting outcomes
  • Contribute to the continuous improvement of consulting methodologies, tools and resources
  • Remain informed of legislative changes and emerging HR and Industrial Relations trends

About You

  • A degree qualification in Human Resources, Business or a related discipline
  • Minimum 4 years' experience in a HR generalist or HR consulting role
  • Strong knowledge of Australian employment legislation, Industrial Relations and HR compliance requirements
  • Experience managing employee relations matters and workplace investigations
  • Exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills
  • A proactive, solutions-focused and commercially minded approach
  • The ability to manage multiple priorities and build strong client relationships
  • High levels of professionalism, accountability and initiative
  • Unrestricted working rights in Australia

What's on Offer?

  • Opportunity to work across a diverse portfolio of clients and industries
  • Exposure to complex and meaningful HR projects
  • Strong mentoring and support from experienced leaders
  • Career progression opportunities within a growing consultancy
  • Ongoing professional development and learning opportunities
  • Flexible working arrangements
  • Collaborative, supportive and high-performing team culture
  • Competitive salary package aligned to experience

If you're an experienced HR professional looking for a role that offers variety, professional growth and the opportunity to make a genuine impact, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today or contact Hannah at a&co Recruitment Partners for a confidential discussion - hannah.lelliott@aandco.au
